points: while checks its condition before every pass; something in the body must change it.
range(a, b) gives a, a+1, …, b−1: b − a values when b ≥ a (none otherwise). range(n) starts at 0.

referenceCard.title: Loops

subtitle: Do it again: until a question turns False, or once for each value.

teach.body:
while condition: checks the condition. If it's True, the indented body runs, then Python goes back and checks again. When the check is False, Python skips past the loop. Something inside the body has to change the condition, or the loop never ends.

k // 2 divides and rounds down, which for positive numbers drops the remainder (7 // 2 is 3).
teach.title: while: repeat while a question is True

teach.body:
for x in something: runs the body once per value, with x set to that value: each character of a string, each item of a list, or each number from range.

range(stop) gives 0 up to stop − 1. range(start, stop) gives start up to stop − 1. range(start, stop, step) counts by step; a negative step counts down. The stop value is never included.

[4, 5, 6] is a list: an ordered collection of values. for n in [4, 5, 6]: visits 4, then 5, then 6. Lesson 5 covers lists in detail.
teach.title: for: once for each value

teach.body:
To add things up: start total = 0 before the loop, do total = total + x inside, and use total after the loop. For multiplying, start at 1. Indentation decides what repeats: indented lines run every pass; the first unindented line after the loop runs once, at the end.

break leaves a loop early; you'll meet it again in later lessons.
